evidence.claim: Comfort Systems USA reported Q1 2026 backlog of $12.45 billion, up from $11.94 billion at December 31, 2025 and $6.89 billion at March 31, 2025; this supports backlog strength but does not alone prove AI-specific backlog purity.
evidence.source_title: Comfort Systems USA Reports First Quarter 2026 Results

evidence.claim: Digital Realty reported Q1 2026 total bookings expected to generate $707 million of annualized GAAP base rent at 100% share, a $1.8 billion annualized GAAP base-rent backlog at 100% share, and management cited the largest hyperscale lease in company history plus hyperscale AI-oriented U.S. capacity.
evidence.source_title: Digital Realty Reports First Quarter 2026 Results

evidence.claim: Caterpillar reported Q1 2026 Power & Energy sales of $7.031 billion, up 22% year over year, and said Power Generation sales increased in large reciprocating engines, turbines and turbine-related services, primarily for data-center applications.

Caterpillar announced a strategic alliance and purchase agreement with American Intelligence & Power and Boyd CAT to support a 2 GW dedicated power platform for hyperscale AI infrastructure, with deliveries scheduled from September 2026 through August 2027.
evidence.source_title: American Intelligence & Power Forms Strategic Alliance with Caterpillar and Boyd CAT to Deploy 2 Gigawatts of Dedicated Power for Hyperscale AI Infrastructure

evidence.claim: EMCOR reported Q1 2026 record quarterly revenues of $4.63 billion and record remaining performance obligations of $15.62 billion, up 32.9% year over year; this supports the backlog/execution relationship but requires more segment detail for AI-specific exposure.
evidence.source_title: EMCOR Group, Inc. Reports First Quarter 2026 Results

evidence.claim: EMCOR's March 2026 investor material identifies Network and Communications as data centers and High-Tech Manufacturing as semiconductors, supporting the mapping to AI-related construction nodes while not yet quantifying AI backlog share.

Equinix stated in its 2026 outlook release that it surpassed 500,000 interconnections globally as enterprises connect AI, cloud and network ecosystems, and referenced xScale lease timing expected in early 2026.
evidence.source_title: Equinix Provides Robust 2026 Outlook Driven by Strong Fourth-Quarter Results and Accelerating Business Momentum

evidence.claim: Equinix annual-report material states it expects to accelerate xScale deployment in the U.S., eventually adding more than 1.5 GW of new capacity, and references AI support through capabilities such as advanced liquid cooling.

Trane Technologies announced an agreement to acquire LiquidStack to expand data-center thermal management across chillers, heat rejection, controls, liquid distribution, direct-to-chip cooling and immersion cooling.
evidence.source_title: Trane Technologies to Acquire LiquidStack to Accelerate End-to-End Data Center Thermal Management Solutions

evidence.claim: Trane Technologies' data-center materials describe LiquidStack as developing advanced liquid-cooling solutions that help data centers support high-density compute, reinforcing the link to AI rack-density cooling needs.

Salesforce reported Q4 FY2026 revenue of $41.5 billion for the fiscal year and said Agentforce and Data 360 ARR exceeded $2.9 billion, up over 200% year over year, including $800 million of Agentforce ARR.
evidence.source_title: Salesforce Delivers Record Fourth Quarter Fiscal 2026 Results

evidence.claim: ServiceNow reported Q1 2026 subscription revenues of $3.671 billion, up 22% year over year, RPO of $27.7 billion, up 25% year over year, and said Now Assist customers spending over $1 million in ACV grew more than 130% year over year.
evidence.source_title: ServiceNow Reports First Quarter 2026 Financial Results

evidence.claim: ServiceNow announced Autonomous Workforce capabilities intended to move AI agents from isolated tasks to governed end-to-end job execution, supporting the mapping to enterprise agentic workflow automation.
evidence.source_title: ServiceNow turns enterprise AI chaos into control with the platform for governed, autonomous work

memory_update.text: FIX should remain in the AI physical-buildout cluster, but its relationship is an inference until technology/data-center and AI-specific backlog contribution is quantified from filings or investor materials.
DLR has strong direct evidence for AI-oriented hyperscale capacity via Q1 2026 record bookings, backlog and management language about hyperscale AI-oriented U.S. capacity.
CAT has unusually explicit AI infrastructure evidence for an industrial name: Q1 2026 Power Generation growth tied primarily to data-center applications plus a 2 GW hyperscale AI power agreement.
EME maps to mission-critical AI data-center buildout and skilled labor, but exact data-center or AI backlog share must be extracted before upgrading from inference to fact.
EQIX maps to AI through interconnection, xScale and advanced cooling, but its exposure is broader enterprise/cloud digital infrastructure rather than a pure AI data-center capacity play.
TT maps to the AI thermal bottleneck after LiquidStack, with direct-to-chip and immersion cooling complementing Trane's broader data-center thermal portfolio.
CRM has measurable enterprise AI monetization evidence through Agentforce and Data 360 ARR; later layers should isolate organic Agentforce growth from Data 360/Informatica contribution.

NOW has measurable AI adoption evidence through Now Assist customers above $1 million ACV and broader Autonomous Workforce positioning, but product efficacy and implementation friction remain important falsification checks.
For the physical-infrastructure names, next layer should normalize AI exposure by revenue/backlog percentage, lead times, margins and customer concentration rather than relying only on thematic fit.
For CRM and NOW, next layer should test whether AI ARR/ACV is incremental paid monetization or packaging/upsell attached to existing platform renewals.

summary: Layer 2B ticker-relationship map for the AI candidate chunk. This chunk splits into two sub-clusters: physical AI infrastructure conversion (FIX, DLR, CAT, EME, EQIX, TT) and enterprise AI monetization (CRM, NOW). Strongest direct AI evidence in this pass appears for DLR, CAT, TT, CRM and NOW based on explicit company disclosures tying demand to AI/data centers/agentic AI. FIX and EME remain relevant chokepoint candidates but need more granular validation of AI/data-center revenue mix, margins and backlog composition versus broader technology, industrial and construction demand.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Pull FIX May 2026 investor presentation and latest 10-Q; extract technology/data-center revenue percentage, modular backlog, customer concentration, margin by segment, and whether management specifically attributes growth to AI data centers rather than broader technology projects.
ticker_relationships.node: Data-center construction execution / mechanical and electrical systems / modular construction
ticker_relationships.relationship: Comfort Systems USA maps to the capex-conversion layer: hyperscaler and AI data-center capex becomes usable compute only after mechanical, electrical, modular, service and commissioning work is completed. Current evidence supports a strong construction/backlog relationship, but exact AI-specific exposure still requires validation.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Track megawatts under construction, percentage pre-leased, lease commencement lag, power availability, incremental development capital, hyperscale customer concentration, and renewal pricing.
ticker_relationships.node: Hyperscale AI data-center capacity / colocation / power-land bottleneck
ticker_relationships.relationship: Digital Realty maps directly to the AI physical-capacity layer. Its leasing, backlog, hyperscale AI-oriented capacity and power-constrained campuses determine how quickly AI demand converts into operational data-center capacity.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Separate durable AI data-center power demand from cyclical oil/gas and industrial power demand; track Power & Energy orders, backlog, lead times, data-center-specific disclosures, emissions/permitting constraints, and margin impact from manufacturing costs.
ticker_relationships.node: Behind-the-meter power / backup generation / prime power for AI data centers
ticker_relationships.relationship: Caterpillar maps to the time-to-power bottleneck. If grid interconnection delays persist, AI data-center operators may rely more on large reciprocating engines, turbines, generator sets, microgrids and related power services.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Use EMCOR Q1 2026 presentation and filings to quantify data-center, network-and-communications, semiconductor and high-tech manufacturing backlog; compare organic growth, margin mix, labor availability and project execution risk.
ticker_relationships.node: Mission-critical electrical/mechanical construction / network and communications / skilled labor bottleneck
ticker_relationships.relationship: EMCOR maps to the buildout labor and execution layer, where mission-critical electrical, mechanical and network infrastructure can gate AI data-center completion. Evidence supports a strong backlog and network/communications relationship, but AI-specific backlog purity is not yet fully proven.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Track xScale megawatt deployment, enterprise AI use cases, AI-related bookings, liquid-cooling availability, power density, interconnection growth, and whether AI workloads lift pricing or capex intensity.
ticker_relationships.node: Interconnection-rich colocation / xScale hyperscale capacity / distributed enterprise AI infrastructure
ticker_relationships.relationship: Equinix maps to AI deployment through interconnection, cloud adjacency, xScale hyperscale deployments and data-center capacity for enterprises and service providers. Exposure is strategic but less pure than power-constrained hyperscale shell capacity because EQIX also serves broad digital infrastructure demand.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Quantify data-center revenue and orders after LiquidStack and Stellar Energy integration; track direct-to-chip deployments, liquid-cooling attach rates, margins, customer wins and whether AI rack density shifts demand from traditional HVAC to liquid systems.
ticker_relationships.node: Data-center thermal management / liquid cooling / heat rejection / controls
ticker_relationships.relationship: Trane Technologies maps to the AI rack-density and cooling bottleneck. The LiquidStack acquisition gives Trane direct-to-chip and immersion-cooling exposure, complementing chillers, heat rejection, controls and central-plant capabilities needed for high-density AI data centers.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Track Agentforce ARR, Data 360 ARR excluding acquired Informatica Cloud ARR, work units, attach rates in large deals, net retention, pricing, customer ROI evidence and risk of AI-native competitors compressing seat-based software economics.
ticker_relationships.node: Enterprise AI monetization / agentic AI applications / CRM data layer
ticker_relationships.relationship: Salesforce maps to the AI demand-validation layer because Agentforce and Data 360 ARR provide measurable enterprise AI monetization evidence beyond product announcements. The thesis depends on paid adoption, retention and expansion rather than infrastructure scarcity.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Track Now Assist ACV, customers above $1 million ACV, renewal/expansion impact, autonomous-workflow case studies, implementation success rates, AI billing transparency and whether customers prefer external AI tools integrated into ServiceNow instead of native Now Assist.
ticker_relationships.node: Enterprise workflow automation / AI agents / AI control tower
ticker_relationships.relationship: ServiceNow maps to enterprise agentic workflow adoption, where AI is monetized through Now Assist, autonomous workflow products and platform expansion. Evidence supports strong AI-related customer spend, but product efficacy, governance, pricing clarity and implementation friction remain key falsification areas.
